assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a theoretical flat-band prediction into an experimentally demonstrated, tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity, and opened the whole field of moire quantum matter. The discovery is concrete, originated in a specific prediction followed by a specific experiment, and has had very broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulating and superconducting states, with Cao as first author. The three-person configuration is defensible, but credit to junior experimental co-authors and to other groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yacoby, Efetov) is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups and the interpretation of flat-band correlated physics is stable, though the nature of the superconducting pairing remains debated. Recognition is timely, about eight years after the experiment.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene is not settled.
Whether the prize should reach experimentalists beyond the lead group is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and rested on the conception and construction of two enormously demanding detectors. It is a clear, central discovery at the energy frontier with lasting impact on all of particle physics.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to the theorists. Credit for the experimental side is spread over thousands of collaborators, but the founding spokespeople and leaders of the proposals are an identifiable, if imperfect, group; Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are plausible, while other leaders (e.g. Gianotti, Incandela, Heuer) could be argued for. The prize rules and the collaboration question remain a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: couplings to many particles measured at the LHC, and the Standard Model interpretation is stable. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Attribution within ATLAS and CMS is unavoidably contentious.
Whether the committee would reward detector conception rather than the discovery announcement is unclear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators gave a new class of quantum matter in which topology of band structure produces protected edge and surface states. It combines a clean theoretical idea with decisive experiments and has had great influence on condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (not on the supplied list); Hasan observed the three-dimensional topological insulator. Choosing three from four listed names leaves out Mele, who was a co-author of the central prediction, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are absent, so the configuration is unstable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups and in several materials; the concept is stable and widely applied. Practical applications remain limited but the discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely disputed, particularly Kane versus Mele and the role of the BHZ proposal.
Overlap with the candidates on QAH (B004, B037) means the three-way split of this topic is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and later the association with a blazar and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy. This is a discovery in the sense of finding something new in nature, with large consequences for astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube, but this is a large collaboration project; a single-name credit is thin, and a fair configuration would likely need to include others (the longlist offers only one name), so I cannot propose a fuller configuration from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established; source identification is still partial. Reasonably mature for the discovery itself, early for the astrophysical interpretation.
uncertainties: Only one credited name; other pioneers (e.g. DUMAND/AMANDA leaders) are not available to be proposed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's precision mapping of CMB anisotropies established the Lambda-CDM parameters with percent-level accuracy and anchored modern cosmology. For someone working on cosmology and dark energy, this is a foundational measurement, though COBE (2006) and Peebles (2019) already recognized neighbouring parts.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page designed key instrumentation and Spergel led the analysis and theory interpretation; this is a reasonable trio, though Wilkinson (deceased) and others such as Hinshaw and Komatsu would also be relevant and Planck competes for credit.
assessment.maturity: Superseded and confirmed by Planck and ground experiments; fully mature, and recognition is not premature, although it risks looking like a late addition to a topic already recognized twice.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier cosmology prizes may weigh against it.
Role of Planck and other teams in credit is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of the trapped-ion quantum computer and its experimental realization with gates, entanglement and simulation gave a leading platform for quantum information. The idea is clear and original, and the experiments have been decisive.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the ion-trap gate; Blatt realized key early experiments with entangled ions and gates, though Wineland (2012 laureate) and Monroe, Kielpinski and others also contributed. The trio is natural but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by multiple groups and commercial efforts; the physics is mature. The 2012 prize for Wineland and the recent circuit prize make the timing and overlap questionable.
uncertainties: Whether Monroe or Wineland-adjacent credit should be reflected.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase show that topology and geometry of gauge connections have observable consequences in quantum mechanics, an idea that reaches from condensed matter to gauge theory. As a theorist I value its conceptual depth and its wide influence.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (Bohm deceased 1992) established the effect; Berry the geometric phase, with Simon, Pancharatnam and others as precursors. Only Aharonov and Berry are available from the credited names, which gives a coherent two-person prize but leaves out Bohm.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades (Chambers, Tonomura, optical Berry phase experiments); very mature, possibly considered late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Bohm is deceased and a joint prize is not possible.
Question whether it is a discovery or a theoretical insight is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid-Mott transition and later quantum gas microscopes, provides a controllable window on strongly correlated matter. It is important and well-realized.
assessment.attribution: Theory by Jaksch, Zoller and Cirac and the first Mott insulator experiment by Greiner and Bloch with Esslinger's fermionic work are decisive; I choose the three experimentalists but the theory credit to Zoller and Cirac would be natural, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent groups; the field is stable. Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and quantum information prizes weighs on novelty.
uncertainties: Allocation between theory proposers and experimentalists is unresolved.
